name: Linacs and cyclotrons for radiotherapy
summary: Medical linacs, proton cyclotrons and synchrotrons, and superconducting magnets/RF are accelerator technology deployed clinically; the Bragg-peak beam delivery rests on accelerator design.

name: Radiotherapy demands on accelerator design
summary: Radiotherapy drives compact, reliable accelerator design: energy variation, FLASH dose rates, gantry-mounted superconducting magnets for proton and carbon-ion therapy.

name: Beam optics in proton therapy gantries
summary: Twiss parameters, emittance and focusing lattices determine spot size, beam transport and pencil-beam scanning in proton and carbon-ion therapy beamlines and gantries.

name: Synchrotron crystallography and XFEL structures
summary: Synchrotron macromolecular crystallography, SAXS and XFEL serial femtosecond crystallography supply most protein structures and time-resolved dynamics.

name: X-ray and ultrafast spectroscopy at light sources
summary: Synchrotron and FEL pulses drive X-ray absorption, photoelectron and pump-probe ultrafast spectroscopies of molecules, extending optical multidimensional spectroscopy to X-ray wavelengths.

name: Operando X-ray probes of catalysts and surfaces
summary: Ambient-pressure XPS, grazing-incidence diffraction and XAS at synchrotrons characterise surface structure and working catalysts in situ.

name: Synchrotron characterisation of battery materials
summary: Operando X-ray diffraction, absorption and tomography at synchrotrons track phase transformations and degradation in electrodes and solid electrolytes.

name: Synchrotron phase-contrast and microtomography
summary: Synchrotron coherent beams enable phase-contrast imaging and microCT, the research precursor of coherence-based X-ray contrast and CT reconstruction methods.

name: Free-electron laser vs. stimulated emission lasers
summary: FEL gain from SASE microbunching is collective stimulated emission by free electrons, analogous to semiconductor laser gain but without bound-state inversion.
breaks: FEL gain is classical bunching in an undulator, tunable and not tied to band gaps or carrier recombination.

name: Cyclotron isotope production for PET
summary: Medical cyclotrons produce short-lived PET radioisotopes such as 18F and 11C, linking accelerator sources and targets to radiopharmaceutical supply.

name: SRF cavities and superconducting magnets with SQUIDs
summary: Superconducting technology (niobium, cryogenics, flux control) is shared by accelerator cavities/magnets and SQUID sensors; SRF cavities also serve as quantum and dark-matter sensors.

name: Superconducting magnets in MRI and accelerators
summary: NbTi superconducting magnet and cryogenic technology developed for accelerators is the basis of clinical MRI magnets; both need field homogeneity and quench protection.

name: Resonances and chaos in beams and fluids
summary: Nonlinear resonances, Hamiltonian chaos and dynamic aperture in storage rings parallel Rossby-wave resonant interactions and predictability limits in atmospheric flow.
breaks: Beam dynamics is conservative Hamiltonian; atmosphere is dissipative and forced.

name: Tomographic reconstruction shared by CT and PET
summary: CT and PET/SPECT both reconstruct images from line integrals via Radon transform, filtered back-projection and iterative statistical methods such as MLEM; PET adds attenuation correction from CT.

name: Image quality, SNR and resolution across modalities
summary: Resolution, contrast-to-noise and point-spread/MTF frameworks, plus Fourier-domain k-space and OCT sampling, unify MRI, ultrasound and optical imaging; photoacoustic reconstruction resembles tomography.

name: MRI and NV/atomic magnetometry share spin resonance
summary: MRI relies on nuclear magnetic resonance and Bloch dynamics; NV and atomic magnetometers use the same spin-precession and Ramsey/spin-echo sequences, and SQUIDs enable ultra-low-field MRI and MEG.

name: Semiconductor photodetectors in PET
summary: Silicon photomultipliers and CdZnTe detectors in time-of-flight PET and gamma cameras are semiconductor p-n junction devices operated in avalanche regimes.

name: Radionuclide therapy and dosimetry
summary: Internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy uses the same absorbed-dose, Monte Carlo transport and radiobiology as external beam; PET/SPECT quantify the uptake.

name: Image-guided radiotherapy and treatment planning
summary: CT supplies electron density for dose calculation and cone-beam CT, MRI-linacs and PET guide targeting; image quality and dose trade-offs are shared.

name: Radiation damage to DNA at molecular scale
summary: Radiobiology of strand breaks and repair, and LET dependence of carbon ions, connects to single-molecule studies of DNA mechanics and repair enzymes.

name: Elastography and tissue mechanics
summary: Ultrasound and MR elastography measure shear-wave speed to infer tissue stiffness, the continuum viscoelasticity that cell and tissue mechanics studies as a driver of mechanotransduction.

name: Optical tweezers and fluorescence microscopy lineage
summary: Biomedical optics and single-molecule biophysics share fluorescence, interferometric detection and light-scattering techniques; OCT coherence gating parallels interferometric nanoscale tracking.

name: Single-molecule FRET and spectroscopy
summary: Single-molecule fluorescence and FRET descend from molecular spectroscopy: Förster dipole coupling, photophysics, and Raman or single-molecule detection, with time-resolved methods probing conformational dynamics.

name: Energy landscapes and rate theory
summary: Protein folding landscapes and potential energy surfaces share Kramers/transition-state rate theory, barrier crossing and funnel concepts; force spectroscopy uses Bell-Evans extensions.

name: Single-molecule force spectroscopy and barrier crossing
summary: Pulling experiments measure barrier heights and rates of unfolding, interpreted via Kramers theory and Bell-Evans models; Jarzynski and Crooks relations recover free energies.

name: Electronic structure meets force fields and ML structure
summary: Quantum chemistry parametrises force fields and QM/MM methods for biomolecules; ML potentials and structure predictors learn from such data.

name: Electron transfer in proteins and Marcus theory
summary: Marcus theory of electron transfer governs biological redox chains in respiration and photosynthesis, with reorganisation energy and tunnelling through protein.

name: Noise and kinetic proofreading at single molecules
summary: Gene-expression noise and kinetic proofreading are stochastic-kinetics ideas observed directly by single-molecule counting and enzyme-turnover measurements.

name: Feedbacks and tipping in living and climate systems
summary: Feedback loops, bistability and noise-induced transitions describe both gene circuits and climate tipping elements such as AMOC collapse and albedo feedback.
breaks: Climate has no replicates and poorly constrained dynamics, unlike controlled biological circuits.

name: Surface chemistry of electrodes and catalysts
summary: Adsorption, interfaces and electrocatalysis govern battery SEI layers, hydrogen storage and fuel cells, linking surface science to energy materials.

name: First-principles design of energy materials
summary: DFT and wavefunction methods predict electrode voltages, ion barriers, thermoelectric band structures and perovskite properties for materials screening.

name: Molecular absorption and the greenhouse effect
summary: Greenhouse forcing arises from vibrational-rotational absorption bands of CO2, H2O and CH4; line strengths and selection rules from spectroscopy feed radiative transfer codes.

name: Photovoltaic carriers and electron-transfer kinetics
summary: Charge separation and recombination in organic and perovskite cells follow Marcus-type electron transfer, paralleling band-based drift-diffusion treatments.
breaks: Inorganic crystalline cells use delocalised bands rather than hopping.

name: Geostrophic rotating stratified flow
summary: Atmosphere and ocean obey the same rotating, stratified primitive equations: geostrophic balance, Rossby waves, Ekman layers and baroclinic instability, with western boundary currents mirroring jets.

name: Ocean heat uptake and climate response
summary: Ocean heat uptake and AMOC set the transient climate response and delay equilibrium warming given by radiative forcing and feedbacks.

name: Circulation, convection and cloud feedback
summary: Hadley circulation, convection and jet shifts control water vapour, lapse rate and cloud feedbacks and thus climate sensitivity.

name: Seismic and ultrasound wave imaging
summary: Seismic tomography and ultrasound imaging both invert travel times and scattered waves in elastic media; elastography uses shear waves just as seismology does, and full-waveform inversion appears in both.

name: Tomography across scales
summary: Seismic travel-time tomography and CT reconstruction solve the same linear inverse problem with regularisation and iterative solvers.
breaks: Seismic rays bend and coverage is sparse, unlike controlled CT geometry.

name: Tsunami and ocean wave propagation from earthquakes
summary: Seafloor earthquakes generate tsunamis and tides and waves share shallow-water wave dynamics, linking source seismology to ocean wave propagation.

name: Geodynamo and rotating convection
summary: Core convection in the geodynamo and atmospheric or oceanic convection are rotating, buoyancy-driven flows controlled by Rossby, Ekman and Rayleigh numbers with Taylor-column constraints.
breaks: Geodynamo includes magnetic Lorentz forces and a much lower Ekman number.

name: Atom-interferometer gravimetry for geophysics
summary: Atom-interferometric and superconducting gravimeters measure gravity variations used in geodesy, mass transport and subsurface density mapping.

name: Membrane elasticity and protein-lipid coupling
summary: Helfrich bending elasticity governs membrane deformation by proteins, channels and motors; mechanosensitive channels bridge molecular structure and membrane mechanics.
